violated_contract: A get-or-create keyed on a natural key, such as a person's display name, must decide whether the record exists in the same transaction that creates it. POST /v1/users/people ran a plain name query and then wrote a new random-id person in a separate write, so two concurrent or retried requests for a new name could both miss the lookup and each create a person, leaving duplicates under one name.
canonical_prevention: Re-check the key with a query inside the Firestore transaction that creates the record, completing every read before the first write, and run it through the shared bounded contention retry. Firestore's serializable transactions then abort a racing create, and its retry returns the record the winner created instead of adding a second one. Guard the read-before-create shape with the strict transaction fixture and pin the race through the real route.
